project: Finding high-Tc superconductors with AI-designed models
summary: Predict Tc for conventional and unconventional superconductors from crystal structure, screen open databases for high-Tc candidates, and probe what the models learn about pairing mechanisms.

stages.name: Direction and plan
stages.detail: Machine learning for superconductors with AI-designed models

stages.name: Compute environment
stages.detail: Training runs on GitHub Actions; setting up this repository and the desktop app

stages.name: Electron–phonon data
stages.detail: 7,582 Alexandria entries kept for training (of 8,253); 1,032 JARVIS entries held out as the locked test set; Tc recomputed with mu* = 0.1

stages.name: Measured-Tc data, including unconventional
stages.detail: 2,123 measured Tc for cuprates, iron-based, heavy-fermion and other oxides (1,395 superconducting) from 3DSC, which matches SuperCon to Materials Project structures; graded anchors for later discoveries

stages.name: Baseline models
stages.detail: Electron-phonon baseline (gradient boosting, composition + structure) and measured-Tc baseline (composition only, 15.0 K on unconventional families) done

stages.name: AI-designed models
stages.detail: Storm 5.0 for conventional superconductors (Storm 4.0 with a 90% range for every prediction), Hurricane 2.0 for unconventional ones and Radar 1.0 to pick between them are in use

stages.name: Locked evaluation
stages.detail: 626 dynamically stable JARVIS materials for electron–phonon; leave-one-family-out tests for unconventional families

stages.name: High-Tc screening
stages.detail: Round 2: 50 conventional candidates (Storm) and 50 unconventional ones (Hurricane) proposed by our AI models from JARVIS-DFT, none reported or predicted before and none made of the elements of a known superconductor. All are unchecked predictions; next: full DFT checks of the top conventional ones

stages.name: Public v0.1
stages.detail: Code, models, results and the candidate shortlist published on GitHub

stages.name: Mechanism analysis
stages.detail: Compare electron–phonon Tc with measured Tc to flag materials phonons can't explain, and test known structure–Tc correlations within families

Storm round 5 (6 ways to give Storm 4.0 a 90% range): best One width on log(1 + Tc), so the range grows with Tc, interval score 7.47 K against 8.02 K for one width for every material, better in 5 of 5 folds; for held-out materials it held the computed Tc 90.0% of the time (84.1% for the tenth with the highest Tc), and half of the ranges are narrower than 1.81 K; adopted as Storm 5.0

Hurricane, round 2 (7 AI-designed candidates): best H12 Hurricane 1.0 + structure types, in two parts [probability times Tc], measured-Tc MAE 10.31 K against 12.70 K for Hurricane 1.0, better in 5 of 5 folds (superconductors 12.29 K against 17.76 K); released as Hurricane 2.0

Screening round 1: Radar 1.0 and Storm 5.0 scored 1,577 metals from JARVIS-DFT after leaving out 306 that others have reported, computed or predicted; 50 candidates published, led by InGa3 at 5.9 K (90% range 2.7–12.1 K)

Screening round 2: Storm 5.0 scored 1,464 metals and Hurricane 2.0 354 compounds that Radar 1.0 sent it, from JARVIS-DFT, after leaving out 809 entries that others have reported, computed or predicted or that share the elements of a known superconductor; 50 conventional and 50 unconventional candidates published. All are predictions that no calculation or experiment has checked; Storm's highest is Ga3Bi at 5.9 K (90% range 2.6–11.9 K); Hurricane's are far less certain: its 90% ranges span a factor of about 10 in Tc

ai_model.name: Storm
ai_model.about: Storm is the project's AI-designed Tc model for conventional, phonon-mediated superconductors; it is trained on DFT electron-phonon data, so it does not cover cuprates, nickelates, iron-based or other unconventional superconductors, which are planned for a separate model, Hurricane. An AI agent (Claude) proposes each design; every candidate is trained and scored with the same composition-grouped cross-validation, and a new version is released only if it beats the current best on average and in at least 4 of the 5 folds, and does not do clearly worse on replicated measured Tc.

changes: Adds 11 physics features proposed by the AI: valence electrons per atom and the distance to Matthias's two Tc peaks, d- and p-block shares, light-atom share, an M^-1/2 phonon scale, a stiffness-over-mass proxy, mass ratio, electronegativity spread and packing fraction
Deeper trees: up to 63 leaves (was 31), at least 10 materials per leaf (was 20)

items.name: vec
items.why: valence electrons per atom; Matthias found Tc peaks near 4.7 and 6.5 in transition-metal compounds

items.name: matthias_d47
items.why: distance of the valence-electron count from the first Matthias peak (4.7)

items.name: matthias_d65
items.why: distance from the second Matthias peak (6.5)

items.name: d_fraction
items.why: share of d-block atoms, a proxy for a high density of states at the Fermi level

items.name: p_fraction
items.why: share of p-block atoms (covalent bonding, as in MgB2 and the A15 compounds)

items.name: light_fraction
items.why: share of light atoms (Z <= 9), which vibrate at high frequency

items.name: inv_sqrt_mass
items.why: composition average of M^-1/2; phonon frequencies scale like M^-1/2 (isotope effect)

items.name: omega_proxy
items.why: M^-1/2 divided by the mean nearest-neighbour distance, a crude stiffness-over-mass frequency scale

items.name: mass_ratio
items.why: heaviest over lightest atomic mass; light atoms in a heavy matrix give separate optical modes

items.name: x_diff
items.why: electronegativity difference, a proxy for ionicity and charge transfer

items.name: packing_fraction
items.why: atomic-sphere volume over volume per atom, a proxy for how compressed the lattice is

model_family.text: Combines boosted trees that learn from about 7,600 materials whose electron–phonon coupling λ and phonon scale ω_log have been computed (the Alexandria set) with a crystal-graph network that learns from the atoms and their neighbours: 0.90 K off on average against the computed Tc of materials it never saw, against 0.97 K for the trees alone. Calibrated to measured Tc, it is off by 1.56 K against experiment (Storm 3.0: 1.61 K). Since Storm 5.0 it also gives a 90% range for every prediction: for materials it never saw, the range held the computed Tc 90% of the time (84% for the tenth with the highest Tc), and half of the ranges are narrower than 1.8 K. Our AI agent designed it.

Reads a material’s composition and crystal structure and gives the probability that it belongs to an unconventional family, then sends it to Hurricane or Storm. It learns from 5,751 SuperCon entries in 3DSC (2,123 unconventional, 3,628 conventional). For parent compounds it never saw it picks the right model 99.5% of the time (balanced accuracy), against 98.2% for a composition-only baseline. Trained without any cuprate, it still sends 100% of cuprates to Hurricane. Our AI agent designed it.

Learns from 2,123 measured Tc values (cuprates, iron-based, heavy-fermion and other oxides; SuperCon with Materials Project structures via 3DSC), including 728 materials that did not superconduct. For compounds whose parent it never saw in training it is off by 10.3 K on average, against 12.7 K for Hurricane 1.0 and 15.0 K for a composition-only baseline. Predicting a whole family it never saw is much harder: trained without any cuprate, it misses cuprates by 34 K. Our AI agent designed it.

hurricane.name: Hurricane
hurricane.about: Hurricane is the project's AI-designed Tc model for unconventional superconductors: cuprates, iron- and nickel-based pnictides and chalcogenides, heavy-fermion compounds and other oxides. No first-principles theory gives their Tc, so it learns from measured Tc (SuperCon, with Materials Project structures, via the 3DSC dataset), including materials that did not superconduct. An AI agent (Claude) proposes each design; candidates are scored with cross-validation grouped by parent compound, and a version is released only if it beats the reference on average and in at least 4 of 5 folds.

items.name: p_cu

inputs.label: Structure types proposed by the AI

items.name: 123_cuprate
items.why: RE Ba2 Cu3 O6+x stoichiometry (YBCO and its rare-earth cousins): two CuO2 planes next to CuO chains

items.name: 214_cuprate
items.why: A2 CuO4 stoichiometry (La2-xSrxCuO4 and relatives): single CuO2 planes in a rock-salt stack

items.name: electron_doped_cuprate
items.why: A2 CuO4 with cerium on the A site (Nd2-xCexCuO4, T' structure): doped with electrons

items.name: Bi_cuprate
items.why: bismuth with strontium, copper and oxygen: the Bi-2201, 2212 and 2223 series

items.name: Tl_cuprate
items.why: thallium-based cuprates, among the highest Tc at ambient pressure

items.name: Hg_cuprate
items.why: mercury-based cuprates, the record-holding Hg-12(n-1)n series

items.name: infinite_layer_cuprate
items.why: A CuO2 with no other charge reservoir: infinite-layer (Sr,Ca)CuO2

items.name: 1111_pnictide
items.why: RE (or alkaline earth) Fe As O/F with one of each: the LaFeAsO family, Tc up to 55 K

items.name: 122_pnictide
items.why: A Fe2 As2 with an alkaline-earth or alkali A: the BaFe2As2 family

items.name: 111_pnictide
items.why: A Fe As with an alkali A: LiFeAs and NaFeAs

items.name: 11_chalcogenide
items.why: Fe with Se, Te or S and no other cation: FeSe and Fe(Se,Te)

items.name: 122_chalcogenide
items.why: an alkali with Fe2Se2: intercalated iron selenides such as KxFe2-ySe2

items.name: nickel_pnictide
items.why: nickel instead of iron in the pnictide or chalcogenide layer: low-Tc cousins such as LaNiAsO

items.name: 115_heavy_fermion
items.why: an f element, a Co, Rh or Ir atom and five In or Ga atoms: the CeCoIn5 family

items.name: 122_heavy_fermion
items.why: an f element with two transition-metal and two Si or Ge atoms: the CeCu2Si2 (ThCr2Si2) family

items.name: nickelate_oxide
items.why: nickel oxides without copper: the nickelate family, in 3DSC mostly non-superconducting

items.name: bismuthate_oxide
items.why: bismuth oxides with Ba or K and no copper: Ba1-xKxBiO3 and BaPb1-xBixO3, Tc up to about 30 K

items.name: ruthenate_oxide
items.why: ruthenium oxides with strontium: Sr2RuO4, a long-debated candidate for unconventional pairing

items.name: cobaltate_oxide
items.why: cobalt oxides with sodium: NaxCoO2, superconducting when hydrated

gnn.name: Graph neural network
gnn.summary: crystal-graph network, AI-designed: weight averaging + Allen–Dynes head + crystal descriptors
gnn.about: A crystal-graph network learns Tc, λ and ω_log straight from the atoms and their neighbours, with no hand-made features. It is scored on the same five folds as Storm, grouped by chemical system.

versions.summary: CGCNN-style message passing on the crystal graph, trained end to end

spec.graph: atoms as nodes; edges to the 12 nearest neighbours within 8 Å, periodic images included
spec.node_inputs: a learned vector for each of 64 elements plus 8 element properties (Z, atomic_mass, X, row, group, atomic_radius, mendeleev_no, valence)
spec.edge_inputs: bond length in 40 Gaussians from 0 to 8 Å
spec.layers: 3 gated message-passing layers (sigmoid gate times softplus message, averaged over neighbours, residual, layer norm), width 64
spec.readout: mean over atoms, then a network with 128 and 64 units (SiLU)
spec.targets: log(1 + Tc), log λ and log ω_log together (loss weights 1, 0.5, 0.5); Tc also via Allen-Dynes from λ and ω_log
spec.training: AdamW, peak learning rate 0.002, weight decay 0.0001, warm-up then cosine decay, 64 crystals per step, 200 epochs, Huber loss; the epoch with the lowest validation Tc error on 10% of the training fold's chemical systems is kept

blend.name: average of the graph network and Storm 1.0

radar.name: Radar
radar.about: Radar is the project's router. From a material's composition and crystal structure it gives the probability that the material belongs to an unconventional family (cuprates, iron- and nickel-based, heavy-fermion and other oxides), and sends it to Hurricane if so and to Storm otherwise. It learns from the SuperCon classes in 3DSC. An AI agent (Claude) proposes each design; candidates are scored with cross-validation grouped by parent compound, and a version is released only if it beats the composition-only baseline on average and in at least 4 of 5 folds.

data.cite: T. Sommer et al., 3DSC - a dataset of superconductors including crystal structures, Sci. Data 10, 816 (2023), doi:10.1038/s41597-023-02721-y; data CC BY 4.0, github.com/aimat-lab/3DSC

changes: Adds measurable crystal structure: crystal system, centring, point-group order, volume per atom, density, layering (anisotropy and c/a) and the f-f spacing

Adds physics features proposed by the AI: the d-electron count of the transition-metal layer from charge balance, the cuprate hole doping p and its Tc dome, the number of CuO2 planes, heavy-metal charge reservoirs, the FeAs/FeSe-type layer, f-electron share and count, magnetic 3d share and a doping indicator
Adds the share of each common element

inputs.label: Composition statistics
inputs.detail: mean, spread, min and max of 8 element properties, plus the number of elements

items.name: crystal system and lattice centring
items.why: seven crystal systems and four centring types, one-hot

items.name: pg_order
items.why: order of the point group, a single number for how symmetric the crystal is

items.name: vpa
items.why: volume per atom

items.name: density
items.why: density from the composition and the volume per atom

items.name: aniso
items.why: longest over geometric mean of the two shorter reduced-cell edges, a measure of layering

items.name: c_over_a
items.why: c/a of the conventional cell for tetragonal and hexagonal crystals (1 for cubic)

items.name: f_spacing
items.why: volume per f-electron atom to the power 1/3, a proxy for the f-f distance that decides whether f electrons stay local (the Hill limit)

inputs.label: Physics features proposed by the AI

items.name: tm_d
items.why: d electrons per transition-metal atom from charge balance (Cu2+ is d9, Fe2+ d6, Ni+ d9); each family's parent compound sits at a characteristic filling and doping moves it away

items.name: p_cu
items.why: holes per Cu from charge balance (negative for electron doping); cuprate Tc rises and falls with it

items.name: dome
items.why: the empirical cuprate dome 1 - 82.6 (p - 0.16)^2 (Presland and Tallon), largest at p = 0.16

items.name: cu_layers
items.why: Cu atoms per formula unit, a proxy for the number of CuO2 planes; Tc rises from one to three planes

items.name: heavy_block
items.why: share of Hg, Tl, Bi and Pb, the heavy-metal charge reservoirs of the highest-Tc cuprates

items.name: fe_based
items.why: iron or nickel together with a pnictogen or chalcogen, the FeAs- or FeSe-type layer

items.name: f_share
items.why: share of atoms with a partly filled f shell (Ce, Yb, U, Pu and others), the local moments of heavy-fermion metals

items.name: f_count
items.why: nominal f-electron count of those atoms

items.name: mag3d
items.why: share of magnetic 3d atoms (V to Cu), a proxy for spin fluctuations

items.name: nonint
items.why: share of non-integer stoichiometry, which marks doped samples

items.name: n_atoms_fu
items.why: atoms per formula unit as written, a measure of chemical complexity

items.name: oxide
items.why: share of oxygen

items.name: chalcogenide
items.why: share of S, Se and Te

items.name: pnictide
items.why: share of P, As and Sb

items.name: halide
items.why: share of F, Cl, Br and I

inputs.label: Element fractions
inputs.detail: the share of each element seen in at least ten training compounds

spec.target: probability that the material belongs to an unconventional family
spec.cv: 5-fold, grouped by parent compound (the Materials Project chemical system)
spec.rule: send to Hurricane if the probability is at least 0.5, otherwise to Storm

pool.rule: metals within 50 meV/atom of the convex hull, non-magnetic, 2 to 4 elements, up to 8 atoms in the cell, elements our training data covers; the list holds the 1,434 that Radar sends to Storm, one per chemical system

screen.rule: only our own finds: nothing that SuperCon, 3DSC, the Alexandria or JARVIS electron-phonon data or our list of others' claims already has, and nothing made of exactly the elements of a known superconductor
screen.caveat: Storm predicts the DFT (Allen-Dynes, μ* = 0.10) Tc of a structure that DFT says is stable or nearly so; a candidate is a prediction until a full electron-phonon calculation and then an experiment check it

pool.what: compounds with no superconductivity record that Radar sends to Hurricane
pool.rule: within 50 meV/atom of the convex hull, a band gap of at most 1 eV, magnetic or not, 2 to 5 elements, up to 40 atoms in the cell, elements Hurricane's training data covers; the list holds the 354 that Radar sends to Hurricane, one per chemical system

check.about: out of fold on the 3DSC entries: of the compounds Hurricane gave at least an even chance, the share that superconduct, against the share among the others

hurricane.caveat: Hurricane learned measured Tc from cuprates, iron-based, heavy-fermion compounds and other oxides; it gives the chance that a compound superconducts and its Tc if it does. Many of these compounds would need doping or pressure, and a candidate is a prediction until an experiment checks it
